goals: Decouple Xaero Minimap and World Map terrain discovery and map-writing radius from Minecraft render distance so a 16-chunk render distance can coexist with an approximately 4-chunk discovery radius.
Preserve Xaero behavior otherwise, including existing map visibility and data, normal nearby discovery, Minimap and World Map sharing, waypoints, radar, navigation, and unrelated UI behavior.
Fail open when durable singleplayer eligibility cannot be trusted so the companion never hides already discovered terrain.
scope: Maintain the exact C1 client-side Fabric companion reconstructed from legacy source checkpoint b025ffc38bb2810c7a472ba73970dd8a7277bac2 and coherent retained checkpoint cc33d33816d92bb6c3205227aec368712c1c9d5a.

Apply an inclusive square or Chebyshev discovery radius, default 4 chunks and configurable from 0 through 32 at client startup, without reading or changing Minecraft render distance and without widening a tighter native Xaero distance.
Preserve the four narrow descriptor-pinned boundaries for World Map live writing, Minimap-owned terrain fetching, singleplayer direct-save reconstruction, and pre-policy Xaero leaf-cache import.
Maintain world-local and dimension-separated discovery history with forced pending transaction and persistent fail-open handling for interrupted, corrupt, unavailable, or mismatched state.

Seed pre-install discovery only from exact frozen hashes of existing .xwmc or .xwmc.outdated cache files and Xaero's native undiscovered sentinel while leaving existing cache textures and map data intact.

exclusions: New implementation, redesign, a successor Canary, or dependency-version expansion during this migration.
Modification, patching, or redistribution of Xaero Minimap, Xaero World Map, XaeroLib, their classes, or their assets; the exact All Rights Reserved binaries remain external references only.
Deleting, rewriting, or concealing existing Xaero map data, grandfathering every pre-generated Anvil chunk, or fabricating missing historical discovery when no durable Xaero cache evidence remains.
Changing Minecraft render distance, waypoint or radar reach, map navigation, zoom, cache rendering, or unrelated Xaero behavior.
Minecraft launch, deployment, Test Slot changes, accepted-baseline changes, Test Instance Manager changes, runtime-profile access, or protected gameplay-instance access during this migration.
Runtime claims about Mixin application, freecam or camera-mod centering, first-start cache-manifest cost, or any other behavior not actually observed with C1.
